question: What causes the 8 missing_future_action failures on the technical-override lane, and does any cause admit a deterministic fix?
claim_scope: Simulator still-image replay over AI-first-pass labels on a dirty working tree. Failure decomposition only; no source change, no release measurement.

method.evidence_proxy: emitted future_actions union over live+pause rows; future actions are derived from TechnicalQualitySignal.issues (pixel-driven probe), so an absent expected future action means the probe did not fire on those pixels

occlusion_recall_misses.reading: labels saw foreground obstruction; the probe does not detect occlusion on these pixels, so avoid_occlusion is never emitted. Detector-recall limitation, same family as EV-CA-EVAL-017 but the recall direction: routing was already measured net-negative, and no occlusion signal exists on these records to route.

exposure_direction_contradictions.reading: labels claim overexposure, but measured pixels are dark (exposure_bias -2.60 and -1.71) and the probe emits increase_exposure. Label-contradicted class: the fix is label revision with pixel evidence, not code; consistent with the EV-CA-EVAL-019 framing-audit policy of not fitting rules to contradicted labels.

sharpness_recall_misses.reading: label claims motion_blur and expects stabilize_camera; the probe's gradient thresholds do not fire on these pixels and no other future action is emitted either. Signal-limited.

decision.reading: All 8 failures are explained by three classes, none of which admits a deterministic lever: 5 detector-recall misses (no signal), 2 label-direction contradictions (revision candidates with pixel evidence), 1 sharpness-recall miss (no signal). With EV-CA-EVAL-014/015/019/022 this closes the failure-class accounting for the still-replay lane: every remaining expectation failure is now attributed to signal-limited detection or label revision.
